title.from: Connect a site's X account with OAuth and keep its keys in SSM
title.to: Connect a site's X account with OAuth, keep its keys in SSM, and guide the owner through setup

description.from:
Part of the scheduled publishing and announcements epic. Design: docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md ("Accounts and keys").

Goal: a site owner, without developer help beyond creating their own X developer app, connects the account the site posts from; the client secret and rotating refresh token live only in SSM SecureString per site and account, never in Git, logs, chat or any screen after entry.

Shape: Administration > Announcements > "X app": client id (shown) and client secret (write-only) saved to `/papyrus/<siteId>/announcements/x/client-secret`; "Connect X account" runs OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE (confidential client), callback on the site's newsroom; scopes `tweet.write tweet.read users.read offline.access` (no media.write); refresh token at `/papyrus/<siteId>/announcements/x/<accountId>/refresh-token`; access token in memory for one post only; refresh writes the new token first under a per-account DynamoDB lock; a failed refresh marks "Needs reconnecting" and pauses; Disconnect calls `POST /2/oauth2/revoke` and deletes the parameter; IAM to the path prefix in the plugin template (nothing by hand); a checklist item confirming X's Automated label linked to a human-run account.

Depends on: the channel framework story.

```gherkin
Feature: A site owner connects the X account the site posts from
  The account and its keys belong to the site owner. We keep them safe and never
  show them again once entered.

  Scenario: Entering the X app's keys
    Given Ryan created an X developer app for MoM
    When Ryan enters its client id and client secret in Administration
    Then the page shows the client id and "Secret saved" but never the secret
    And the secret is not in any log

  Scenario: Connecting the account
    When Ryan chooses "Connect X account" and approves MoM at X as @mom_test
    Then Administration shows "Connected: @mom_test"
    And the permissions asked for were posting, reading, the account's profile and staying signed in

  Scenario: Tokens refresh without help
    Given a connected account whose access token has expired
    When an announcement is posted
    Then a new access token is obtained and the new refresh token is saved before posting

  Scenario: Two posts at once do not break the connection
    Given two announcements post at the same moment
    Then only one refresh happens and both posts use its token

  Scenario: A broken connection pauses and says so
    Given X refuses to refresh the token
    Then the account shows "Needs reconnecting"
    And announcements for the site pause with that reason

  Scenario: Disconnecting
    When Ryan chooses "Disconnect"
    Then the token is revoked at X and deleted from our store
    And announcements stop

  Scenario: The automated label is confirmed before turning on
    Given a connected account
    When Ryan turns announcements on
    Then Ryan must first confirm "This account shows X's Automated label, managed by a person's account"
```

Open questions: the X help pages on automation and labels could not be fetched by tool; a person should read them before MoM goes live.
description.to:
Part of the scheduled publishing and announcements epic. Design: docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md ("Accounts and keys").

Goal: a site owner, following a plain-language guide (docs/x-announcements-setup.md, drafted on the plan PR) and the same steps shown in the product, connects the account the site posts from; the client secret and rotating refresh token live only in SSM SecureString per site and account, never in Git, logs, chat or any screen after entry.

Shape: the setup steps from docs/x-announcements-setup.md shown on the page with the exact callback URL and a Copy button (a paid X subscription gives no API access; the developer app has its own prepaid credits); Administration > Announcements > "X app": client id (shown) and client secret (write-only) saved to `/papyrus/<siteId>/announcements/x/client-secret`; "Connect X account" runs OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE (confidential client), callback on the site's newsroom; scopes `tweet.write tweet.read users.read offline.access` (no media.write); refresh token at `/papyrus/<siteId>/announcements/x/<accountId>/refresh-token`; access token in memory for one post only; refresh writes the new token first under a per-account DynamoDB lock; a failed refresh marks "Needs reconnecting" and pauses; Disconnect calls `POST /2/oauth2/revoke` and deletes the parameter; IAM to the path prefix in the plugin template (nothing by hand); a checklist item confirming X's Automated label linked to a human-run account.

Depends on: the channel framework story.

```gherkin
Feature: A site owner connects the X account the site posts from
  The account and its keys belong to the site owner. We keep them safe and never
  show them again once entered.

  Scenario: The page explains the setup in plain words
    Given an owner who has never used X's developer site
    When the owner opens Administration > Announcements
    Then the page lists the steps: create an X developer app, choose OAuth 2.0 "Read and write" for a web app or bot, paste the callback URL shown, buy credits and set a spending limit, paste the keys, connect
    And the callback URL has a Copy button
    And the page says a paid X subscription does not include API access

  Scenario: Entering the X app's keys
    Given Ryan created an X developer app for MoM
    When Ryan enters its client id and client secret in Administration
    Then the page shows the client id and "Secret saved" but never the secret
    And the secret is not in any log

  Scenario: Connecting the account
    When Ryan chooses "Connect X account" and approves MoM at X as @mom_test
    Then Administration shows "Connected: @mom_test" (the account's real handle)
    And the permissions asked for were posting, reading, the account's profile and staying signed in

  Scenario: Tokens refresh without help
    Given a connected account whose access token has expired
    When an announcement is posted
    Then a new access token is obtained and the new refresh token is saved before posting

  Scenario: Two posts at once do not break the connection
    Given two announcements post at the same moment
    Then only one refresh happens and both posts use its token

  Scenario: A broken connection pauses and says so
    Given X refuses to refresh the token
    Then the account shows "Needs reconnecting"
    And announcements for the site pause with that reason

  Scenario: Disconnecting
    When Ryan chooses "Disconnect"
    Then the token is revoked at X and deleted from our store
    And announcements stop

  Scenario: The automated label is confirmed before turning on
    Given a connected account
    When Ryan turns announcements on
    Then Ryan must first confirm "This account shows X's Automated label, managed by a person's account"
```

Open questions: does MoM's X account exist yet, and its handle (Ryan)? The X help pages on automation and labels could not be fetched by tool; a person should read them before MoM goes live.
